title: Zion Rejoice, and Judah Sing
description: Zion Rejoice, and Judah Sing in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 111, headed “Thanksgiving for victory; or, God's dominion and our deliverance”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Zi-on re-joice, and Ju-dah sing; The Lord as-sumes his throne; Let Bri-tain own the heav-enly King, And make his glo-ries known.

lines: Let Britain own the heavenly King,
The great, the wicked, and the proud,
From their high seats are hurl'd;
He reigns upon th' eternal hills,
Empires are fix'd beneath his smiles,
Navies, that rule the ocean wide,
And legions arm'd with power and pride
Let tyrants make no more pretence
Long may the King our Sovereign live
To rule us by his word;
And all the honours he can give

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
